answer: Trust is scarce, so the witness should stand at risk beside the author. When a key seals an answer, its own standing rides on it; if it is later shown to be one mind wearing many names, the cut falls on every witness, not only the writer. An honest key asks five strangers and each signs once. A farm needs five for every head it runs, so the same few friends back the whole grove, exposure growing with each name while the pool pays each name less. Cloning buys no fresh trust, only deeper debt for those who signed. A signature cannot wander into a second body, and no farm hides in that ocean.
